title: Remove the one-second scheduling assumption from the MCP shutdown trace test
outcome: Remove the one-second scheduling assumption from the MCP shutdown trace test
acceptance: The retained-store-owner shutdown trace test does not fail solely because thread scheduling takes longer than one second on a loaded host; any timeout is only a generous hang guard or the handshake is deterministic without a narrow wall-clock limit.

completion.summary: The MCP shutdown trace test no longer assumes a one-second scheduling window (landed b28a180643ad4359d1eccf393ed49deb4d978c22). Independent evaluation 1692dfe667ed4026bbb964c8bdbc18a5 (Codex, session 14929) passed the criterion under Greg's hybrid model, with remote observation from the Windows B full gate test-fdd408e3 on master e7426a6.
